title: The Historians’ Most Perfect Song
synopsis: Learn about a masterpiece of Chinese history and the trials overcome by its author.

fullText.simplified:
史家绝唱

    中国的皇帝们，除了自己的名字以外，还有一些封号。比如说，第一位皇帝刘邦被称作“汉高祖”，据说是因为他很高尚；刘隆出生不到一百天就当了皇帝，不到一岁就死了，他被称为“汉殇帝”，“殇”就是很小就死了的意思；刘彻又叫“汉武帝”，据说是因为他很勇敢，很英武，打败了匈奴——但是，这个“武”字，也是“武断”的“武”。
    汉武帝的一生几乎都在打仗，攻克了匈奴，扩大了国土。等到老了，他却因为睡不好觉，就觉得有人在诅咒自己，为此杀了很多人。如果说，这样还不能算“武断”，也许我们可以来说说另一件事。
    李陵是汉朝的将军，受汉武帝任命去攻打匈奴。他一个人偷偷去了敌人后方，想要一下子抓住他们。但是，他一时失误，还没来得及动手，就被匈奴发现并俘虏了。
    这个消息传到皇宫里，许多人都说：“这个李陵，他现在不去死，一定是要投降，去做匈奴人的将军！”汉武帝听了别人的话，真的以为李陵对匈奴投降了。他愤怒极了，就打算杀掉李陵全家。
    司马迁是一个记录历史的小官，他和李陵是好朋友。他不忍心看到这样的事情，就对皇帝说：“虽然这次输了，但是李陵先前多次攻克敌人，已经值得大家记在心里。他现在投降，没有去死，应该是在等待机会。如果有机会，他肯定还会力求反击。”
    汉武帝并不相信司马迁的话。在他心中，李陵投降就是背叛，再也不是他的大将军。而司马迁这个家伙，竟然还为李陵说好话。汉武帝更生气了。他立刻杀了李陵的全家，还把司马迁关进了监狱。
    远方的李陵知道自己的家人全死了，心里非常绝望，再也不愿意为汉武帝做事，就真的向匈奴投降了。
    这事还没结束。汉武帝心中的怒火久久不能平息。他决定用宫刑来惩罚司马迁——也就是说，叫人割了司马迁的生殖器。这样的惩罚太残酷，太霸道了！
    在古代，只有皇帝的下人才需要这样。他们要照顾皇帝和他的妻子们，皇帝们不能忍受一个真正的男人陪伴自己的女人，所以就把这些下人都变得不是男人。而司马迁并不是一个下人。他出身在读书人的家里，从小就爱学习，他的家人、朋友都在当官，自己也有一个体面的官职。现在，他被惩罚了，变得不像男人，也不像女人。这真是一个巨大的侮辱。
    受完了惩罚，司马迁的身体疼痛无比，不知道自己能不能活下来。他的精神也很痛苦，不知道自己活下来还能做什么。但司马迁没有一直沉溺在伤心、苦闷之中，他被关在监狱，也没有忘记自己的工作。他想起父亲的梦想是写出一本中国历史的书，就决定继承父亲的梦想，写下从遥远的古代到汉朝的历史。
    于是，他用了整整十三年，不论是在黑暗、狭窄的监狱，还是出狱后面对着外界的嘲笑和指指点点，司马迁都没有停止过写作。终于，他写出了一部不朽的《史记》。
    这本《史记》，包含了中国三千多年的历史，从遥远的古代到汉朝，从皇帝、将军到普通人，一共有52万字。司马迁冷静地回顾着三千年历史，查阅了大量的资料，分析这些历史事件是怎么发生的，又是怎么结束的。他也公正地评价着这些历史中的人，甚至是当时的汉武帝。他不怕汉武帝生气，不怕受更多的惩罚，也不怕死。因为只有这样，他才能写出真实、公正的历史。
    司马迁勇敢、正直、关心朋友，更有着锲而不舍的精神。他的《史记》一直都是公认的最优秀、最有道理的历史著作，在中国有着举足轻重的地位。著名作家鲁迅曾赞美《史记》是“史家之绝唱，无韵之离骚”。到了今天，学中国历史的人还会依靠这本书来了解那三千年中发生了什么。

史家絕唱

    中國的皇帝們，除了自己的名字以外，還有一些封號。比如說，第一位皇帝劉邦被稱作“漢高祖”，據說是因為他很高尚；劉隆出生不到一百天就當了皇帝，不到一歲就死了，他被稱為“漢殤帝”，“殤”就是很小就死了的意思；劉徹又叫“漢武帝”，據說是因為他很勇敢，很英武，打敗了匈奴——但是，這個“武”字，也是“武斷”的“武”。
    漢武帝的一生幾乎都在打仗，攻克了匈奴，擴大了國土。等到老了，他卻因為睡不好覺，就覺得有人在詛咒自己，為此殺了很多人。如果說，這樣還不能算“武斷”，也許我們可以來說說另一件事。

    這個消息傳到皇宮裡，許多人都說：“這個李陵，他現在不去死，一定是要投降，去做匈奴人的將軍！”漢武帝聽了別人的話，真的以為李陵對匈奴投降了。他憤怒極了，就打算殺掉李陵全家。

sentences.pinyin: tā lì kè shā le lǐ líng de quán jiā hái bǎ sī mǎ qiān guān jìn le jiān yù
sentences.english: Yet this guy Sima Qian was still speaking up for Li Ling. Emperor Wu became even angrier.
He immediately killed Li Ling’s entire family and also locked Sima Qian up in prison.

sentences.simplified: 远方的李陵知道自己的家人全死了，心里非常绝望，
sentences.traditional: 遠方的李陵知道自己的家人全死了，心裡非常絕望，
sentences.pinyin: yuǎn fāng de lǐ líng zhī dào zì jǐ de jiā rén quán sǐ le xīn li fēi cháng jué wàng

sentences.simplified: 再也不愿意为汉武帝做事，就真的向匈奴投降了。
sentences.traditional: 再也不願意為漢武帝做事，就真的向匈奴投降了。
sentences.pinyin: zài yě bú yuàn yì wèi hàn wǔ dì zuò shì jiù zhēn de xiàng xiōng nú tóu xiáng le
sentences.english: When Li Ling, who was far away, found out that his entire family was dead, he was filled with despair.
He never wanted to work for Emperor Wu again and actually surrendered to the Xiongnu.

sentences.simplified: 这事还没结束。汉武帝心中的怒火久久不能平息。
sentences.traditional: 這事還沒結束。漢武帝心中的怒火久久不能平息。
sentences.pinyin: zhè shì hái méi jié shù hàn wǔ dì xīn zhōng de nù huǒ jiǔ jiǔ bù néng píng xī

sentences.simplified: 他决定用宫刑来惩罚司马迁——也就是说，叫人割了司马迁的生殖器。
sentences.traditional: 他決定用宮刑來懲罰司馬遷——也就是說，叫人割了司馬遷的生殖器。
sentences.pinyin: tā jué dìng yòng gōng xíng lái chéng fá sī mǎ qiān yě jiù shì shuō jiào rén gē le sī mǎ qiān de shēng zhí qì
sentences.english: It doesn’t end here. Emperor Wu’s anger could not be quelled for a very long time.

sentences.simplified: 这样的惩罚太残酷，太霸道了！
sentences.traditional: 這樣的懲罰太殘酷，太霸道了！
sentences.pinyin: zhè yàng de chéng fá tài cán kù tài bà dào le
sentences.english: He decided to punish Sima Qian with castration—that is, he had someone cut off Sima Qian’s genitals.
This punishment was so cruel and despotic!

sentences.simplified: 在古代，只有皇帝的下人才需要这样。
sentences.traditional: 在古代，只有皇帝的下人才需要這樣。
sentences.pinyin: zài gǔ dài zhǐ yǒu huáng dì de xià rén cái xū yào zhè yàng

sentences.simplified: 他们要照顾皇帝和他的妻子们，
sentences.traditional: 他們要照顧皇帝和他的妻子們，
sentences.pinyin: tā men yào zhào gù huáng dì hé tā de qī zi men
sentences.english: In ancient times, only the emperor’s servants needed to do this.

sentences.simplified: 皇帝们不能忍受一个真正的男人陪伴自己的女人，所以就把这些下人都变得不是男人。
sentences.traditional: 皇帝們不能忍受一個真正的男人陪伴自己的女人，所以就把這些下人都變得不是男人。
sentences.pinyin: huáng dì men bù néng rěn shòu yí ge zhēn zhèng de nán rén péi bàn zì jǐ de nǚ rén suǒ yǐ jiù bǎ zhè xiē xià rén dōu biàn de bú shì nán rén
sentences.english: They had to take care of the emperor and his wives.

sentences.simplified: 而司马迁并不是一个下人。他出身在读书人的家里，从小就爱学习，
sentences.traditional: 而司馬遷並不是一個下人。他出身在讀書人的家裡，從小就愛學習，
sentences.pinyin: ér sī mǎ qiān bìng bú shì yí ge xià rén tā chū shēn zài dú shū rén de jiā lǐ cóng xiǎo jiù ài xué xí
sentences.english: The emperors could not have real men accompany his women, so he made sure his servants were no longer men.

sentences.simplified: 他的家人、朋友都在当官，自己也有一个体面的官职。
sentences.traditional: 他的家人、朋友都在當官，自己也有一個體面的官職。
sentences.pinyin: tā de jiā rén péng you dōu zài dāng guān zì jǐ yě yǒu yí ge tǐ miàn de guān zhí
sentences.english: However, Sima Qian was not a servant. He came from a family of scholars and had loved studying since he was a child.

sentences.simplified: 现在，他被惩罚了，变得不像男人，也不像女人。这真是一个巨大的侮辱。
sentences.traditional: 現在，他被懲罰了，變得不像男人，也不像女人。這真是一個巨大的侮辱。
sentences.pinyin: xiàn zài tā bèi chéng fá le biàn de bú xiàng nán rén yě bú xiàng nǚ rén zhè zhēn shì yí ge jù dà de wǔ rǔ
sentences.english: His family and friends were all officials, and he himself also held a respectable official position.
Now, he was punished, so he was neither a man nor a woman. This truly was a huge insult.

sentences.simplified: 受完了惩罚，司马迁的身体疼痛无比，不知道自己能不能活下来。
sentences.traditional: 受完了懲罰，司馬遷的身體疼痛無比，不知道自己能不能活下來。
sentences.pinyin: shòu wán le chéng fá sī mǎ qiān de shēn tǐ téng tòng wú bǐ bù zhī dào zì jǐ néng bù néng huó xià lai

sentences.simplified: 他的精神也很痛苦，不知道自己活下来还能做什么。
sentences.traditional: 他的精神也很痛苦，不知道自己活下來還能做什麼。
sentences.pinyin: tā de jīng shén yě hěn tòng kǔ bù zhī dào zì jǐ huó xià lai hái néng zuò shén me
sentences.english: After suffering this punishment, Sima Qian’s body was in immense pain, and he didn’t know if he would survive.

sentences.simplified: 但司马迁没有一直沉溺在伤心、苦闷之中，他被关在监狱，也没有忘记自己的工作。
sentences.traditional: 但司馬遷沒有一直沉溺在傷心、苦悶之中，他被關在監獄，也沒有忘記自己的工作。
sentences.pinyin: dàn sī mǎ qiān méi yǒu yì zhí chén nì zài shāng xīn kǔ mèn zhī zhōng tā bèi guān zài jiān yù yě méi yǒu wàng jì zì jǐ de gōng zuò
sentences.english: He was also in psychological pain, not knowing what he could do with his life if he survived.

sentences.simplified: 他想起父亲的梦想是写出一本中国历史的书，
sentences.traditional: 他想起父親的夢想是寫出一本中國歷史的書，
sentences.pinyin: tā xiǎng qǐ fù qīn de mèng xiǎng shì xiě chū yì běn zhōng guó lì shǐ de shū
sentences.english: But Sima Qian didn’t wallow in his sadness. He didn’t forget his work even when locked up in prison.

sentences.simplified: 就决定继承父亲的梦想，写下从遥远的古代到汉朝的历史。
sentences.traditional: 就決定繼承父親的夢想，寫下從遙遠的古代到漢朝的歷史。
sentences.pinyin: jiù jué dìng jì chéng fù qīn de mèng xiǎng xiě xià cóng yáo yuǎn de gǔ dài dào hàn cháo de lì shǐ
sentences.english: He remembered that his father’s dream was to write a book on Chinese history.
So, he decided to carry on his father’s dream and record history from the distant ancient times up until the Han Dynasty.

sentences.simplified: 于是，他用了整整十三年，
sentences.traditional: 於是，他用了整整十三年，
sentences.pinyin: yú shì tā yòng le zhěng zhěng shí sān nián

sentences.simplified: 不论是在黑暗、狭窄的监狱，还是出狱后面对着外界的嘲笑和指指点点，
sentences.traditional: 不論是在黑暗、狹窄的監獄，還是出獄後面對著外界的嘲笑和指指點點，
sentences.pinyin: bú lùn shì zài hēi àn xiá zhǎi de jiān yù hái shi chū yù hòu miàn duì zhe wài jiè de cháo xiào hé zhǐ zhǐ diǎn diǎn
sentences.english: Consequently, he spent a full 13 years on this.

sentences.simplified: 司马迁都没有停止过写作。
sentences.traditional: 司馬遷都沒有停止過寫作。
sentences.pinyin: sī mǎ qiān dōu méi yǒu tíng zhǐ guò xiě zuò
sentences.english: Whether it was in the dark, cramped prison, or facing the ridicule and judgment of the outside world after his release, ..

sentences.simplified: 终于，他写出了一部不朽的《史记》。
sentences.traditional: 終於，他寫出了一部不朽的《史記》。
sentences.pinyin: zhōng yú tā xiě chū le yí bù bù xiǔ de shǐ jì
sentences.english: .. Sima Qian never stopped writing.
Finally, he completed the monumental work “Records of the Grand Historian”.

sentences.simplified: 这本《史记》，包含了中国三千多年的历史，
sentences.traditional: 這本《史記》，包含了中國三千多年的歷史，
sentences.pinyin: zhè běn shǐ jì bāo hán le zhōng guó sān qiān duō nián de lì shǐ

sentences.simplified: 从遥远的古代到汉朝，从皇帝、将军到普通人，一共有52万字。
sentences.traditional: 從遙遠的古代到漢朝，從皇帝、將軍到普通人，一共有52萬字。
sentences.pinyin: cóng yáo yuǎn de gǔ dài dào hàn cháo cóng huáng dì jiāng jūn dào pǔ tōng rén yí gòng yǒu 3 wàn zì
sentences.english: This work, “Records of the Grand Historian”, contains more than 3,000 years of China’s history.

sentences.simplified: 司马迁冷静地回顾着三千年历史，
sentences.traditional: 司馬遷冷靜地回顧著三千年歷史，
sentences.pinyin: sī mǎ qiān lěng jìng de huí gù zhe sān qiān nián lì shǐ
sentences.english: From the distant ancient times to the Han Dynasty, and from emperors to generals, and to commoners, it has a total of 520,000 characters.

sentences.simplified: 查阅了大量的资料，分析这些历史事件是怎么发生的，又是怎么结束的。
sentences.traditional: 查閱了大量的資料，分析這些歷史事件是怎麼發生的，又是怎麼結束的。
sentences.pinyin: chá yuè le dà liàng de zī liào fēn xī zhè xiē lì shǐ shì jiàn shì zěn me fā shēng de yòu shì zěn me jié shù de
sentences.english: Sima Qian soberly reviewed 3,000 years of history.

sentences.simplified: 他也公正地评价着这些历史中的人，甚至是当时的汉武帝。
sentences.traditional: 他也公正地評價著這些歷史中的人，甚至是當時的漢武帝。
sentences.pinyin: tā yě gōng zhèng de píng jià zhe zhè xiē lì shǐ zhōng de rén shèn zhì shì dāng shí de hàn wǔ dì
sentences.english: He consulted a large number of sources, analyzing how each of these historical events occurred and how they ended.

sentences.simplified: 他不怕汉武帝生气，不怕受更多的惩罚，也不怕死。
sentences.traditional: 他不怕漢武帝生氣，不怕受更多的懲罰，也不怕死。
sentences.pinyin: tā bú pà hàn wǔ dì shēng qì bú pà shòu gèng duō de chéng fá yě bú pà sǐ
sentences.english: He also evaluated the people throughout history without bias, even the then Emperor Wu.

sentences.simplified: 因为只有这样，他才能写出真实、公正的历史。
sentences.traditional: 因為只有這樣，他才能寫出真實、公正的歷史。
sentences.pinyin: yīn wèi zhǐ yǒu zhè yàng tā cái néng xiě chū zhēn shí gōng zhèng de lì shǐ
sentences.english: He was not afraid of angering Emperor Wu. He was not afraid of further punishment, nor was he afraid of death.
Because only this way could he write a true and fair history.

sentences.simplified: 司马迁勇敢、正直、关心朋友，更有着锲而不舍的精神。
sentences.traditional: 司馬遷勇敢、正直、關心朋友，更有著鍥而不捨的精神。
sentences.pinyin: sī mǎ qiān yǒng gǎn zhèng zhí guān xīn péng you gèng yǒu zhe qiè ér bù shě de jīng shén

sentences.simplified: 他的《史记》一直都是公认的最优秀、最有道理的历史著作，
sentences.traditional: 他的《史記》一直都是公認的最優秀、最有道理的歷史著作，
sentences.pinyin: tā de shǐ jì yì zhí dōu shì gōng rèn de zuì yōu xiù zuì yǒu dào li de lì shǐ zhù zuò
sentences.english: Sima Qian was brave and honest, and he cared for his friends. Moreover, he had a spirit of perseverance.

sentences.simplified: 在中国有着举足轻重的地位。
sentences.traditional: 在中國有著舉足輕重的地位。
sentences.pinyin: zài zhōng guó yǒu zhe jǔ zú qīng zhòng de dì wèi
sentences.english: His “Records of the Grand Historian” has long been recognized as the most outstanding and most plausible historical work.

sentences.simplified: 著名作家鲁迅曾赞美《史记》是“史家之绝唱，无韵之离骚”。
sentences.traditional: 著名作家魯迅曾讚美《史記》是“史家之絕唱，無韻之離騷”。
sentences.pinyin: zhù míng zuò jiā lǔ xùn céng zàn měi shǐ jì shì shǐ jiā zhī jué chàng wú yùn zhī lí sāo
sentences.english: It has had an influential position in China.

sentences.simplified: 到了今天，学中国历史的人还会依靠这本书来了解那三千年中发生了什么。
sentences.traditional: 到了今天，學中國歷史的人還會依靠這本書來了解那三千年中發生了什麼。
sentences.pinyin: dào le jīn tiān xué zhōng guó lì shǐ de rén hái huì yī kào zhè běn shū lái liǎo jiě nà sān qiān nián zhōng fā shēng le shén me
sentences.english: The famous writer Lu Xun praised “Records of the Grand Historian” as “the historians’ most perfect song, a ‘Li Sao’ without the rhyme”.

sentence_translations: The Historians’ Most Perfect Song
As well as their own names, the emperors of China had several other titles.
For instance, it is said that the first emperor Liu Bang was called “Emperor Gaozu of Han” because he was morally upright.
Liu Long became emperor less than 100 days after he was born but died before he turned one year old.
He was given the name “Emperor Shang of Han”, with “shang” meaning died at a very young age.
It is said that Liu Che was also called “Emperor Wu of Han” because he was very courageous and martial, and defeated the Xiongnu.
But, this “wu” character also appears in “wuduan” [arbitary].
Emperor Wu was at war for almost his entire life. He overcame the Xiongnu and expanded his country’s territory.
However, because he didn’t sleep well when he became old, he thought that people were putting curses on him.
He killed many people because of this.
If this doesn’t count as “arbitrary”, perhaps we can discuss another incident.
Li Ling was a general of the Han Dynasty and was appointed by Emperor Wu to attack the Xiongnu.
He secretly went behind the enemy, wanting to capture them all at once.
However, he made a mistake and was discovered and captured by the Xiongnu before he had the chance to do anything.
This news made its way to the imperial palace.
Many people said, “This Li Ling, if he doesn’t die now, it must be because he plans to surrender and become a general for the Xiongnu!”
Emperor Wu heard what other people said and actually believed that Li Ling had surrendered to the Xiongnu.
He was extremely angry and decided to kill Li Ling’s entire family.
Sima Qian was a minor official who recorded history. He and Li Ling were good friends.
He couldn’t bear to see such a thing happen, so he told the emperor:
“Even though we lost this time, Li Ling’s many previous successful attacks on the enemy are worthy of being remembered.
The fact that he is surrendering now rather than going to die must be because he is waiting for an opportunity.
If he gets the opportunity, he will definitely make every effort to strike back.”
Emperor Wu did not believe Sima Qian.
In his mind, Li Ling’s surrender was a betrayal. Li Ling would never again be his great general.
Yet this guy Sima Qian was still speaking up for Li Ling. Emperor Wu became even angrier.
He immediately killed Li Ling’s entire family and also locked Sima Qian up in prison.
When Li Ling, who was far away, found out that his entire family was dead, he was filled with despair.
He never wanted to work for Emperor Wu again and actually surrendered to the Xiongnu.
It doesn’t end here. Emperor Wu’s anger could not be quelled for a very long time.
He decided to punish Sima Qian with castration—that is, he had someone cut off Sima Qian’s genitals.
This punishment was so cruel and despotic!
In ancient times, only the emperor’s servants needed to do this.
They had to take care of the emperor and his wives.
The emperors could not have real men accompany his women, so he made sure his servants were no longer men.
However, Sima Qian was not a servant. He came from a family of scholars and had loved studying since he was a child.
His family and friends were all officials, and he himself also held a respectable official position.
Now, he was punished, so he was neither a man nor a woman. This truly was a huge insult.
After suffering this punishment, Sima Qian’s body was in immense pain, and he didn’t know if he would survive.
He was also in psychological pain, not knowing what he could do with his life if he survived.
But Sima Qian didn’t wallow in his sadness. He didn’t forget his work even when locked up in prison.
He remembered that his father’s dream was to write a book on Chinese history.
So, he decided to carry on his father’s dream and record history from the distant ancient times up until the Han Dynasty.
Consequently, he spent a full 13 years on this.
Whether it was in the dark, cramped prison, or facing the ridicule and judgment of the outside world after his release, ..
.. Sima Qian never stopped writing.
Finally, he completed the monumental work “Records of the Grand Historian”.
This work, “Records of the Grand Historian”, contains more than 3,000 years of China’s history.
From the distant ancient times to the Han Dynasty, and from emperors to generals, and to commoners, it has a total of 520,000 characters.
Sima Qian soberly reviewed 3,000 years of history.
He consulted a large number of sources, analyzing how each of these historical events occurred and how they ended.
He also evaluated the people throughout history without bias, even the then Emperor Wu.
He was not afraid of angering Emperor Wu. He was not afraid of further punishment, nor was he afraid of death.
Because only this way could he write a true and fair history.
Sima Qian was brave and honest, and he cared for his friends. Moreover, he had a spirit of perseverance.
His “Records of the Grand Historian” has long been recognized as the most outstanding and most plausible historical work.
It has had an influential position in China.
The famous writer Lu Xun praised “Records of the Grand Historian” as “the historians’ most perfect song, a ‘Li Sao’ without the rhyme”.
Even to this day, those who study Chinese history still rely on this book to understand what happened in those 3,000 years.
